problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{3x-{x}^{2}}{5{x}^{4}-4}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Horizontal Asymptote When the Degree of the Denominator is Greater
examples.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{3x^2+ 2x}{6x^4-1}$.
examples.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to\infty.$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is $x^4.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by $x^4,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x}{6{x}^{4}-1} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{6{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})}{(6-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms  $\dfrac{3}{x^2}, \dfrac{2}{x^3},$ and $\dfrac{1}{x^4}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to\infty,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})}{(6-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0}{6-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y = 0.$

feedback.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{4{x}^{2}+6x+1}{1-2{x}^{2}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

In this case, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{2}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{4{x}^{2}+6x+1}{1-2{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{4{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{6x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{(4+\frac{6}{x}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{6}{x}$ and $\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(4+\frac{6}{x}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-2)} \\  & \to \frac{4+0+0}{0-2} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is  $y=-2.$
